lines.text: One quarter brought Macy's about 35% of fiscal 2025 sales.
lines.say: One quarter brought Macy's about thirty-five percent of fiscal twenty twenty-five sales.

lines.text: That's $7.6 billion of $21.8 billion, and it's where Macy's keeps the least of each sale.
lines.say: That's seven point six billion out of twenty-one point eight, and it's where Macy's keeps the least of each sale.

lines.text: Gross margin, what's left after product costs, ran about 39% in other quarters, then 35.2% in the holiday quarter.

lines.text: In general, doorbusters are priced thin, sometimes below cost, to pull shoppers in.

post.title: One quarter, 35% of Macy's sales: the Black Friday math
post.ig:
One quarter brought Macy's about 35% of its fiscal 2025 sales.

Macy's holiday quarter (Nov 2025-Jan 2026): $7.6B of $21.8B in fiscal 2025 net sales.
Its gross margin rate was 39.2%, 39.7% and 39.4% in Q1-Q3, then 35.2% in Q4. Macy's attributed Q4's 0.5-point year-over-year decline mainly to about 0.6 points of tariff impact.
Hypothetical doorbuster: a TV that cost $300 sells for $280 (-$20), plus $100 of add-ons at a 40% margin (+$40) = +$20 basket.
Retailers expected 17% of 2025 holiday sales to be returned.

Sources: Macy's, Inc. FY2025 10-K and quarterly results (2025-2026); NRF and Happy Returns, 2025 Retail Returns Landscape (Oct 2025).

Macy's holiday quarter brought in $7.6 billion of its $21.8 billion fiscal 2025 net sales, about 35%, but its gross margin dropped to 35.2% from about 39% in the first three quarters (Macy's attributed most of Q4's year-over-year decline to tariffs). Doorbusters work on the whole basket, and retailers expected 17% of 2025 holiday sales to be returned. Sources: Macy's, Inc. FY2025 10-K and earnings releases; NRF and Happy Returns 2025 Retail Returns Landscape (Oct 2025).

News and education, not financial advice.
